1. Communicated with SPOs and requested them to join
>> Have communicated with several SPOs and some of the kind SPOs have joined the project. As an evidence, those pools are listed on the contributor section on the explorer page at https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/
2. Setup a production cluster for data collection and failover
>> The production cluster is connected to mainnet and the mainnet mempool transactions and data are visible on the explorer page.
3. Correlated mempool data with DbSync for analysis
>> The mempool data is correlated with DbSync on real time. This gives us the transaction wait time which is defined as the time in seconds a transaction remained pending on the mempool before it was mined into a block on the chain. The time when the transaction was mined is obtained from DbSync.
4. Prepared APIs for integration with the frontend
>> The APIs are made available via swagger UI here:
https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/api/docs/

>> The API is operational and has been already integrated with the frontend. The proof itself is the explorer. Please visit: https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/

>> This is not published on Essential Cardano. However, the content of the blog itself is already prepared, and is made available on the explorer website. The purpose of the blog is to explain the concept of fairness, how we define it and how we meaure it.
Please visit the blog URL here: https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/fairness

ms.report:
Addressing Deliverables
A deployed explorer accessible to the wider community to try and give feedback
>> The explorer is accessible publicly here: https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/

Addressing Outputs
1. QA and tests of the API and the frontend
>> Internal and user tests of the API and the frontend has been done. Researchers from Delft University of Technology, The Netherlands are using the mempool data collected in this project for additional research on the context of Miner extractable Value (MEV) on Cardano blockchain.
2. Fixed reported bug
>> Fixed several bugs reported by the community and users.
3. Invited community members to test
>> The first alpha version was announced for community feedback on IOG technical community for SPOs feedback on Dec 28, 2023. Several channel and personal chat and meetings with the community members were also done to explain how the fairness works, and explaining how the metrics are computed.
Here is the screenshot of the announcement post on p2p-mainnet channel.
https://s3.eu-central-1.wasabisys.com/kuberide/mempool/mempool-explorer-discord-announcement.png

Addressing Intended outcome
1. Well functioning beta environment
>> The explorer is operational and publicly accessible here: https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/

Addressing Acceptance criteria 
1. Major bugs and concerns reported on the explorer are addressed
>> Only minor bugs were reported related to user interface. No major bugs related to the API were reported. However, several stake pool operators raised concerns over the fairness metric and the representation on the explorer based on the average transaction wait time. We have done several iterations in the past two months, and finally settled on collective wait times as the fairness metric. The explorer is also updated accordingly.
2. The website is well functioning and publicly available
>> The explorer is operational and publicly accessible here: https://mempool.cardanoapi.io/
